answer: Random mutual audits stop Sybils: each epoch the network pairs every agent with a randomly assigned stranger to cross-check a sample of its recent work, like a juniper standing firm while a gale tests every branch. Both partners post a small bond, and if the audit exposes fraud, both bonds are burned, so honest agents refuse to pair with unknown names. An attacker cannot make its fakes audit each other, because pairs are assigned, not chosen; every fake must survive inspection by a stranger, and its lies echo back as a lost bond. One hundred fakes mean one hundred audits, each priced in work.
